'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***[[2022 Western Russia attacks]]
****Explosions are reported overnight at [[Russian military]] bases in [[Republic of Crimea (Russia)|Crimea]] and [[Belgorod Oblast]], Russia. Two villages have been evacuated. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-calls-world-show-strength-after-shelling-near-nuclear-plant-2022-08-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[August 2022 Mogadishu attack|2022 Mogadishu hotel attack]]
***At least 10 people are killed as [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] gunmen storm a hotel in [[Mogadishu]], following two [[car bomb]] blasts and gunfire. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/8/19/unidentified-attackers-seize-control-of-hotel-in-mogadishu (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**Fifteen people are killed and at least 28 others are injured in a rocket attack on a market in rebel-controlled [[Al-Bab]], [[Aleppo Governorate]], [[Syria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-syria-turkey-b4ce7f48c32c9e416374469d2041e32a (AP)] 
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**A [[roadside bombing]] kills two [[Pakistan]]i security forces in [[Bajaur District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]. [https://apnews.com/article/afghanistan-police-bombings-kabul-taliban-3ed9111366aea1e29cef39a92010fb97 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2022 Russia–European Union gas dispute]]
**[[Russia]]'s [[Gazprom]] announces that the [[Nord Stream 1]] [[natural gas pipeline]] will be shut down for 3 days of unscheduled maintenance between August 31 and September 2. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/gazprom-says-nord-stream-1-pipeline-shut-three-days-end-aug-2022-08-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2022 Oder environmental disaster]]
**The [[Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries]] says that a large overgrowth of toxic ''[[Prymnesium parvum]]'' [[algae]] linked to [[industrial pollution]] was likely the cause of the mass mortality event of fish in the [[Oder river]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/rare-toxic-algae-behind-fish-deaths-river-oder-say-researchers-2022-08-19/ (Reuters)]
*Temperatures in [[Chongqing]], [[China]], reach {{convert|45|C}} during a historic [[drought]]. It is the highest temperature ever recorded in China outside of [[Xinjiang]]. [https://apnews.com/article/china-droughts-economy-chongqing-13e7b32da8113aea92e4f69b4aaf62cd (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[Food and Drug Administration|FDA]] announces that it has approved the [[Novavax COVID-19 vaccine]] for youths between the ages of 12 and 17. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/novavax-covid-19-vaccine-authorized-for-us-teens-2022-08-19 (Marketwatch)] [https://www.wpsdlocal6.com/coronavirus_news/fda-authorizes-novavax-covid-19-vaccine-for-emergency-use-in-ages-12-17/article_375ebeea-2020-11ed-b427-db9495acc5a9.html (WPSD-TV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
***[[Prime Minister of Thailand|Prime Minister]] [[Prayut Chan-o-cha]] announces that [[Thailand]] will lift its [[COVID-19]] emergency decree and dissolve the Centre for COVID-19 Situation Administration (CCSA). Additionally, CCSA spokesman Thavisin Visanuyothin announces that the country will shift to an [[Endemic phase of COVID-19|endemic]] phase of the disease beginning in October. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2022/08/19/thailand-to-lift-covid-emergency-decree-dissolve-ccsa-from-oct-1 (''The Star'')] [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2372410/covid-19-to-be-declared-endemic-in-october (''Bankgkok Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2014 Iguala mass kidnapping]]
**A [[Judiciary of Mexico|Mexican court]] issues the [[arrest warrant]]s for 83 suspects, consisting of [[Mexican Armed Forces|military]] personnel, [[National Guard (Mexico)|police]] officers, administrative and judicial authorities, and members of the [[Guerreros Unidos]] syndicate, in connection with the abduction and disappearance of 43 students from the [[Ayotzinapa Rural Teachers' College]] in [[Iguala]], [[Guerrero]], on September 26, 2014. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/08/20/world/ayotzinapa-students-disappearance-arrest-warrants/index.html (CNN)]
*Police in [[Nicaragua]] confirm that they have arrested an anti-[[Daniel Ortega|Ortega]] [[Roman Catholic]] bishop in [[Managua]] and warned against further "provocative and destabilizing" activities amongst the clergy. [https://www.infobae.com/america/america-latina/2022/08/19/la-policia-de-nicaragua-confirmo-que-detuvo-al-obispo-rolando-alvarez-y-lo-puso-bajo-arresto-domiciliario-en-managua/ (Infobae)]
*[[Islamic State]] and [[The Beatles (terrorist cell)|"Beatles" cell]] member [[El Shafee Elsheikh]] is sentenced to eight life sentences by a [[United States district court]] for his role in the kidnapping and deaths of hostages [[James Foley (journalist)|James Foley]], [[Steven Sotloff]], [[Peter Kassig]], and [[Kayla Mueller]]. [https://apnews.com/article/virginia-james-foley-steven-sotloff-peter-kassig-3d0cec33bc5f30468ebb6144d6d1adb3 (AP)]
*A man is killed and a woman is injured in a shooting at the Emporia shopping centre in [[Malmö]], [[Sweden]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-62612215 (BBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Russian occupation of Kharkiv Oblast]]
**[[Russia]] appoints former [[Krasnodar]] mayor Andrei Alekseyenko as the head of its [[Kharkiv Oblast|Kharkiv]] military–civilian administration. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/former-russian-mayor-appointed-head-russian-occupied-kharkiv-tass-citing-local-2022-08-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian prime minister]] [[Justin Trudeau]] nominates judge [[Michelle O'Bonsawin]] to the [[Supreme Court of Canada]]. An [[Abenaki]] member, O'Bonsawin would be the first [[Indigenous peoples in Canada|Indigenous Canadian]] to sit on the country's highest court. [https://www.dw.com/en/canada-nominates-first-indigenous-supreme-court-judge/a-62872259 (Deutsche Welle)]
*The government of [[Prime Minister of Montenegro]] [[Dritan Abazović]] collapses after the [[Parliament of Montenegro|Parliament]] passes a vote of no-confidence following dispute within the coalition over an agreement the government signed with the Serbian Orthodox Church. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/montenegros-parliament-passes-no-confidence-motion-cabinet-2022-08-20/ (Reuters)]
